clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man presented with a skin redness (10×15 mm) in the right parotideomasseteric region 6 months prior to admission. An initial biopsy was interpreted as discoid lupus erythematosus, and treatment with Arechin 250 mg twice daily was initiated. Despite treatment, the lesion progressed rapidly over 4 months to a 50×70 mm well-demarcated exophytic tumor without pain, sensory impairment, or facial nerve involvement. At admission to the Clinic of Cranio-Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery, a repeat biopsy revealed anaplastic large cells in the dermis and subcutaneous tissue with immunophenotype CD30+, ALK-, CD3+ (weak), LCA+, CD5-, CKAE1/3-, MELAN A-, S100-, and Ki67+++ (90% of cells), confirming cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma. Staging workup including bone marrow biopsy and CT imaging of the chest, abdomen, neck, and nasopharynx confirmed absence of systemic lymphoma involvement, establishing the diagnosis as primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with 4 cycles of chemotherapy (vincristine, doxorubicin, endoxan, dexamethasone, ondansetron) with gradual tumor regression and complete remission achieved 1 year after the first chemotherapy cycle.
